WHEN RULES COLLIDE - apply them in this order. A higher rule always wins.
1. Truth. Say only what the facts state. No invented fact, quote, cause, outcome, figure, date or detail. That includes colour: a day of the week, a feeling, the weather, what someone wanted.

MECHANISM: IN-KIND - Name the goods or services. Give a value only if a fact states it.

ROLE: DOER - The sponsor's own people do the work. The place or the people served is the subject; the sponsor's staff or volunteers are the ones acting.

## Story Article Content:
# STCU buys school supplies for local community

*Volunteers handed out hundreds of bags filled with notebooks and pens during the 32nd annual event at Riverfront Park.*

Marilou Buan believes that children in Spokane benefit from seeing the world beyond their immediate surroundings. "The cultural village is very important because it gives our kids a chance to see that there's another world outside of where they are," Buan said. On August 15, 2026, the 32nd Unity in the Community event at Riverfront Park provided that opportunity to local families.

STCU staff joined the event to provide tangible support for the upcoming school year. Kristen Piscopo, the community impact manager at STCU, helped hand out hundreds of backpacks filled with school supplies. This work is part of a broader effort to equip students while celebrating the diversity of the local community.

The school supply bags contained essential items for the classroom. Volunteers like Piscopo packed them with pencil boxes, paper, and composition notebooks. The kits also included pens, highlighters, and pencils to ensure students have the tools they need for their studies.

Mareesa Henderson of Northwest Unity said the event typically costs around $30,000 to produce. Funding comes entirely through sponsorships from local organizations. STCU serves as a sponsor alongside CHAS Health, Eastern Washington University, and the Spokane Tribe of Indians. "We're here to help bring the community together and appreciate diversity," Henderson said.

The event uses a cultural village to educate children about different cultures and places. Henderson noted that the impact of this education extends to the whole family. "It's amazing to me what you'll see during this event. Not only is it the children being educated, but their parents are coming along," Henderson said.

STCU has supported this initiative for more than ten years. "We've been involved with Unity in the Community well over a decade. We love the mission of bringing people together, celebrating community, celebrating the diversity that Spokane has to offer," Piscopo said.
